newsitem.title: UK: LME metals sparkle, zinc and nickel stand out.
newsitem.headline: LME metals sparkle, zinc and nickel stand out.

text.p: LME metal prices were on the boil on Wednesday afternoon as zinc extended its fund-led run to a 23-month high and nickel scored its strongest level this year.
Flagship copper held steady but had trouble generating fresh momentum as traders and speculators poured money into other metals.
Wednesday's gains pushed Flemings Global Mining Group's base metal index to 119.5, the highest since June 3 last year, analyst Nick Moore said.
The index is 19 percent off its low hit in October, he added.
Three month zinc prices shot up to a high of $1,132 per tonne, the strongest since February 3, 1995, as stops were hit, floor traders said.
The kerb close was up $13 at $1,122 per tonne and on the cusp of the technically important $1,123/4 area, the top of a two-year sideways trading range.
Zinc was playing catch-up, having been ignored recently, but Chinese selling and profit-taking may soon eat into the rally that had gained $52 in two days, traders said.
"It's had quite a good run, but I think it's done enough for now," one said.
Nickel pushed above recent peaks, touching $7,420, the highest since October 29, 1996 after stops were triggered above $7,320/30, floor traders said.
The market, which has gained nearly $800 or 12 percent since the New Year, has along with zinc been a favorite of investment funds.
Three months prices finished the kerb $190 stronger and just off the high at $7,410.
Copper consolidated in a recent range as players put it on the back burner. It showed resilience, however, by recovering from a test lower to $2,240. It ended the kerb $1 up at $2,262.
Aluminium added a few dollars, but shyed away from challenging $1,625 highs hit Monday and Tuesday.
Analysts expect sideways movement near-term as it works off overbought levels ahead of a fresh upside attack. Prices ended the day $9 higher at $1,617.
Tin added to its recent rally, gaining $40 to $6,075 by the end of afternoon business. The $6,100 level was critical, since a break above there would spark fund short-covering, one floor trader said.
Lead ended the day $8 firmer at $716, but still needs to breach the December high of $723 before more progress can be made, chartists said.
Alloy was last indicated slightly lower at $1,508/10 versus $1,515.
